ai.description: This gecko reaches 7–9 cm. It is pale brown or grey with dark, chevron-shaped dorsal markings. Key features include adhesive toe pads and a distinct, dark line extending from the snout through the eye.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Lepidodactylus lugubris* is best identified by the distinct dark, chevron-shaped markings along its back and the presence of small, fleshy flaps along its hind limbs.
ai.habitat: Mourning geckos inhabit tropical coastal areas and human-modified landscapes, typically found on coconut palms and fruit trees from sea level up to 500 meters in elevation.
ai.behavior: Mourning geckos are primarily nocturnal, emerging at night to hunt small insects and lap up nectar or fruit juices from their environment.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Lepidodactylus lugubris* is an obligate parthenogenetic species that lays clutches of two hard-shelled, adhesive eggs. They breed year-round in tropical Indian habitats.
ai.distributionRemarks: Lepidodactylus lugubris occurs in coastal regions of India, including the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, typically inhabiting low-elevation tropical environments.
